proof_attempt_summary: The run derived the action-marked finite-information experiment, bounded-information impossibility, the Gaussian frontier, zero-visit-safe inversion, and a raw-reward crossover construction; the independent math review passed. The package nevertheless remained subfield-tier because its upper theory is confined to the two-state model and the unrestricted-kernel inversion lacks certified finite-dimensional computation. A field-tier successor must re-anchor around a broader-class upper theorem or a computable sharp procedure, while also repairing the empty-candidate fallback and literature positioning.
tldr: From one randomized two-state trajectory, the stationary evaluation value is identified by the joint reward-transition kernel. Finite transition information leaves nonvanishing uncertainty; with diverging transition information, a raw-reward exact-inversion interval is honest on every sample and has the local Gaussian-quantile diameter whenever the crossover variance is positive, even when \(T\gamma_T=\log\log T\).
gap: Regular average-reward efficiency and one-path stationary-functional intervals do not settle inference when the mixing time grows with the observation horizon and some state rewards are unseen.
fill: Establish the joint information phase diagram and an exact interval whose high-information length matches the transition efficiency bound at nonzero state-reward contrast.
